title: Central diagonalizable quotients from character sublattices
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $H$ be a split semisimple $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] with split maximal torus $T_H$, character lattice $X_H$, roots $R_H$ and coroots $c_\alpha$, in the conventions of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]; semisimple means smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup. Let $C$ be a free abelian group of finite rank and put $A=H\times_F D_F(C)$, $T_A=T_H\times_F D_F(C)$ and $X=X_H\oplus C$. Here $D_F(B)=\operatorname{Spec}F[B]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $B$, with group algebra basis $e^b$, product $e^be^{b'}=e^{b+b'}$, comultiplication $e^b\mapsto e^b\otimes e^b$, counit $e^b\mapsto1$, and antipode $e^b\mapsto e^{-b}$. Let $N\subseteq X$ be a finite-index subgroup containing $(\alpha,0)$ for every $\alpha\in R_H$. Under $T_A\simeq D_F(X)$ the quotient $X\to X/N$ defines a closed subgroup $K=D_F(X/N)\hookrightarrow T_A$. Then $K$ is finite and central in $A$, and the fppf quotient $G=A/K$ is a smooth connected affine reductive $F$-group scheme of finite type. The fppf quotient means the sheafification of $B\mapsto A(B)/K(B)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented algebra coverings. Its quotient map $q:A\to G$ is faithfully flat with scheme-theoretic kernel $K$. The image $S=q(T_A)=T_A/K$ is a split maximal torus, and pullback identifies $X^*(S)$ with $N\subset X$. Under this identification its roots are precisely the elements $(\alpha,0)\in N$, and their coroots are $c^N_\alpha(n)=c_\alpha(\operatorname{pr}_{X_H}n)$ in $\operatorname{Hom}(N,\mathbf Z)$. Finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra; central means commuting with all points after every scalar extension. These assertions include $H=1$, $C=0$, $N=X$, and kernels whose order is divisible by $\operatorname{char}F$.

source.place: Exercise 21-4, printed p.461; central-product construction 19.26--19.27, printed pp.404--405; centre as common root kernel, Section 21a; central isogeny root/coroot comparison, Proposition 23.5, pp.485--486. This is the equivalent finite-central-quotient construction starting with a weight-lattice semisimple group and a torus.

proof.text: Write $Z=D_F(C)$. A basis of $C$ identifies $Z$ with a split torus by [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria]. The projection $Z\times H\to H$ is smooth by [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection], and [lem-trf-smooth-composition] makes $A$ smooth over $F$. The same torus-projection statement says that $L[C]$ is a domain for every field extension $L/F$, so $Z$ is geometrically connected. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components] and connectedness of $H$ make $A$ connected. Its identity is an $F$-point, so [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] makes $A$ geometrically connected. Its coordinate algebra is $F[H]\otimes_F F[C]$, generated by the generators of $F[H]$ and the basis characters of $C$ and their inverses. Thus $A$ is affine and of finite type.

source.place: Examples 12.1--12.2 and Proposition 12.3, pp.231--232; product group geometry as in 19.26--19.27, pp.404--405. Smooth composition: Stacks Tag 01VA, morphisms-lemma-composition-smooth; connected products: Tag 0385, varieties-lemma-bijection-connected-components; rational point: Tag 04KV, varieties-lemma-geometrically-connected-if-connected-and-point.

proof.text: The semisimple group $H$ is reductive by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $W\subseteq A$ be a smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. The projection $A\to H$ is faithfully flat: $F[H]\otimes F[C]$ is a free $F[H]$-module with the nonempty basis $(e^c)_{c\in C}$, and tensoring is a nonempty direct sum of copies, hence is exact and detects zero modules. Factor $W\to H$ through its faithfully flat image using [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image]. By [lem-sfb-unipotent-normal-quotient-image] this image is smooth connected normal and unipotent, and therefore trivial in $H$. The projection $W\to Z$ is trivial by [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial]. Both projections of the inclusion $W\hookrightarrow H\times Z$ are thus trivial, so the inclusion factors through the identity and $W=1$. This proves that $A$ is reductive.

source.place: Definition 19.9, p.399; Theorem 5.39, p.108; Corollaries 14.7 and 14.18(a), pp.282--284; projection argument for a product with a torus.

proof.text: The torus $T_A=T_H\times Z$ is split. To check maximality, let $J\subseteq A$ be a torus containing it. Factor the projection $J\to H$ using [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image]; its image is a torus by [lem-sfb-torus-homomorphism-image] and contains $T_H$. The maximality of $T_H$ makes that image exactly $T_H$. Thus $J\subseteq T_H\times Z=T_A$, proving maximality. A character on a product is the product of its restrictions, since $(t,z)=(t,1)(1,z)$. Together with [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], this identifies $X^*(T_A)=X_H\oplus C=X$ and $T_A=D_F(X)$.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(a)--(c), pp.233--234; 12.14, p.236; product maximal tori in Exercise 21-4, p.461.

proof.text: The surjection $X\to X/N$ induces the closed immersion $K\hookrightarrow T_A$ by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality]. The basis $(e^{\bar x})_{\bar x\in X/N}$ of $F[X/N]$ is finite, so $K$ is finite. For every root $\alpha$ of $H$, the character $(\alpha,0)$ restricts to the zero class in $X/N$, since $(\alpha,0)\in N$. Thus the projection $K\to T_H$ factors through the common scheme-theoretic root kernel, which equals $Z(H)$ by [lem-sfb-reductive-centre-root-quotient]. The other projection lands in the commutative factor $Z$. Hence $K\subseteq Z(H)\times Z\subseteq Z(A)$, so $K$ is central and normal. This is a statement on all test algebras, including nonreduced ones, because the root restriction is the identity character in the group algebra, not just an identity on $F$-points.

Apply [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] to the affine finite-type group $A$ and its normal closed subgroup $K$. It represents precisely the stated fppf sheaf quotient by an affine finite-type group $G$, and supplies a faithfully flat finitely presented quotient map $q:A\to G$ with scheme-theoretic kernel $K$. Since $A$ is smooth and geometrically connected, that statement makes $G$ smooth and geometrically connected, hence connected.

source.place: Theorem 5.28, pp.104--105; Section 5(j), pp.116--118; Proposition 1.62(b), p.24; Proposition 5.59(b), p.114.

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq G$ be smooth connected normal and unipotent. It is solvable by [lem-sfb-smooth-unipotent-solvable]. Apply [lem-sfb-central-isogeny-solvable-normal-lift] to $q$ and $U$: the source and target are smooth connected affine groups of finite type, and the kernel is finite central by step 4. This gives a smooth connected solvable normal subgroup $V\subseteq A$ mapping faithfully flatly onto $U$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-radical-quotient], $V$ lies in the radical $R(A)$, which is a central torus because $A$ is reductive. Over the algebraically closed $F$ this torus is split, so [lem-sfb-split-torus-subgroups-diagonalizable] makes its closed subgroup $V$ diagonalizable, say $D_F(M)$. The smooth unipotent group $U$ has a closed immersion into an upper unitriangular group by [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-unitriangular-embedding]. Now [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-to-unipotent-trivial] makes $V\to U$ trivial as a group-scheme map. A trivial faithfully flat map onto $U$ forces $U=1$ (the induced injection $F[U]\hookrightarrow F[V]$ factors through $F$). Thus $G$ is reductive.

source.place: Radical argument of Corollary 17.62(b), pp.372--373; Proposition 6.27, p.131; Theorem 14.5 and Corollaries 14.12, 14.18(b), pp.281--284; quotient construction 19.26--19.27, pp.404--405.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-quotient-borel-torus-images], $S=q(T_A)$ is a split maximal torus of $G$ and $q_T:T_A\to S$ is faithfully flat. Its scheme-theoretic kernel is $K$, since $K\subseteq T_A$. The affine fppf quotient $Q=T_A/K$ exists by [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry]. Apply [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-group-quotient-universal] to $q_T$ and to $T_A\to Q$: each factors uniquely through the other because their kernels agree; uniqueness makes the resulting two maps inverse. Thus $S=T_A/K$ as fppf quotients. The same universal-property node, with target $\mathbf G_m$, identifies characters of $S$ with characters of $T_A$ trivial on $K$. Under [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], restriction $X^*(T_A)\to X^*(K)$ is exactly $X\to X/N$. Consequently $q_T^*$ is injective with image exactly $N$.

source.place: Proposition 17.20, pp.357--358; Theorem 5.13, p.101; Theorem 12.9(a),(c), pp.233--234; Exercise 21-4, p.461.

proof.text: Choose a Borel pair of $G$ using [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], and conjugate its torus to $S$ using [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy]; this gives a Borel pair $(B,S)$. Apply [lem-sfb-central-isogeny-borel-root-compatibility] to $q:A\to G$. Its inverse-image torus $q^{-1}(S)$ contains $T_A$ and is maximal, so equals $T_A$. For the product $A=Z\times H$ (interchanging the two factors), the product clause of that statement identifies the roots and coroots at this torus with those of $H$ at the given $T_H$. Thus the roots upstairs are $(\alpha,0)$ and the coroot functional upstairs evaluates $x\in X$ as $c_\alpha(\operatorname{pr}_{X_H}x)$. The same statement says that pullback identifies the roots and preserves the integer coroot pairing. Using step 7, each root downstairs is therefore the element $(\alpha,0)\in N$, and its coroot evaluates $n\in N$ as $c_\alpha(\operatorname{pr}_{X_H}n)$, as claimed. These are integral character and cocharacter identities; no differential or separability of $q_T$ is used.
